title: Add air-gapped integration test harness for offline bundle verification (no network, test key)
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: We’ve added offline bundle signature + checksum verification in the installer (PRs #1042/#1049) and the break-glass override flow (PR #1051). We were missing an end-to-end integration test that proves verification works in a truly offline context (no outbound calls) and fails closed when integrity checks fail. This PR adds a hermetic “air-gapped” integration test harness that (1) generates a minimal offline bundle fixture (manifest + payload), (2) signs it with a non-production test key, (3) runs `redwood-private-installer verify-bundle` and `install` preflight in a network-blocked environment, and (4) asserts on exit codes + structured log fields for auditability. Goal: prevent regressions that only show up in customer labs (e.g., relying on network access for key retrieval, timestamps, or registry lookups) and cover the common failure reported in SUP-18421 (manifest digest mismatch after transfer). What changed (high level): - Added `tests/integration/airgap/` harness that orchestrates fixture build + verification runs. - Added a test-only signing key + public cert under `tests/fixtures/keys/` (explicitly marked DO NOT USE IN PROD). - Added `airgap_netns` helper that executes verification inside a Linux network namespace with no interfaces + DNS disabled (falls back to `unshare -n` when running in privileged CI). - Added negative-path cases: tampered payload (checksum mismatch), tampered manifest (signature mismatch), and downgrade attempt (bundle version < required minimum) to assert fail-closed behavior. - Wired up GitHub Actions job `integration-airgap` (Linux only) to run on PRs touching `cmd/verify`, `internal/verify/*`, or installer workflows. Notes/constraints: - The harness does not attempt to pull any images or reach any registries. The fixture is a local directory bundle (tar) to keep the test fast and deterministic. - We avoid embedding private material beyond the test key; the test key is only used to validate that our verification path works, not to validate KMS/HSM integration. - For portability, the test harness skips (with a clear message) when kernel features required for network namespaces are unavailable; CI is configured to run in an environment where they are available. Follow-ups: - Once the KMS-backed signer is enabled in the staging pipeline, add a nightly job that verifies a real staged bundle using the published public key set (tracked in ENG-3920/ENG-3913).
commits: test(integration): add air-gapped harness runner and fixtures
test(keys): add test signing keypair and documentation warning
verify: expose stable error codes and log fields for integration assertions
ci: add integration-airgap GitHub Actions job
docs: add developer notes for running airgap tests locally
ci_summary: Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), integration-airgap (pass), gosec (pass). Reruns: integration-airgap rerun once after tightening namespace teardown to avoid leaked processes.
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we ensure this test never reaches out to fetch the public key set from config defaults? We should be explicitly passing the key path into verify so we don’t silently depend on network later. Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated harness to invoke `verify-bundle --public-key-path tests/fixtures/keys/TESTING_SIGNING_PUB.pem` and to assert `verification.key_source=local_file` in structured logs. Added a guard that fails the test if the installer tries to read from the default keyring directory. Marcus Lin (review): Please add loud labeling around the test private key and ensure it’s not in any release artifacts. Also, we should validate we fail closed when signature verification can’t be performed (e.g., missing key). Benji Okafor (author): Added header comments + README note; key lives only under `tests/fixtures/` and excluded from release packaging by existing goreleaser config (verified). Added a new test case `missing_public_key_fails_closed` asserting exit code `RPI_VERIFY_0102` and log `verification.result=error` with `verification.fail_closed=true`. Irene Choi (review): Network namespace setup tends to be flaky in CI. If it flakes, we’ll end up ignoring it. Can we make the harness deterministic and clean up namespaces reliably? Benji Okafor (author): Switched to `unshare -n` invocation for the verification subprocess and added explicit process group kill + deferred cleanup. Also added a preflight that checks `CLONE_NEWNET` availability and prints actionable skip reasons. Kevin Osei (review): For auditability, we should assert on the exact fields we emit (bundle id, manifest sha256, signature key id). Benji Okafor (author): Added assertions for `bundle.manifest_sha256`, `bundle.signature_key_id`, `bundle.bundle_id`, and the verification outcome. This should align with the structured logging changes in #1049 and upcoming export work (ENG-3920). Approvals: Ethan Park approved. Marcus Lin approved after key labeling + fail-closed case. Irene Choi approved after cleanup change. Merge: Squash merged into main.
release_notes: Private installer: added hermetic air-gapped integration tests for offline bundle verification to prevent regressions in offline/regulated environments.
